content.title: Olivia Rodrigo's New Album Title Breaks A Longstanding Tradition
content.text: Album cover for Olivia Rodrigo's upcoming third album.Olivia rodrigo/xOlivia Rodrigo announced her third studio album, you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love will be released on June 12.That is ten words. Her previous albums were SOUR (2021) and GUTS (2023) — both four letters, both capitalized, both one-word gut punches. Fans had spent months guessing what four-letter title would come next. Speculation ranged from "LOVE" (after the word appeared on a teaser mural in Los Angeles) to "GOLF" (after a cryptic photo of a golf cart with "the album" written on it surfaced in January) to "LUCK." The Olivia Rodrigo fan wiki had been calling the project "OR3" as a placeholder and noted that "it's more than likely that the title of this album will follow the pattern of previous albums and be a one-word, four-letter, capitalized title."It did not.Rodrigo shared the news and cover art on Instagram today, writing, "my third album 'you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love’ is out June 12th. I am so proud of this record and I can’t wait for you to hear it." The cover shows her in a pink outfit on a swing, also a departure from her previously purple-themed work. She also wiped her entire Instagram feed before the announcement, leaving only the album post.What To Know About The AlbumThe record was produced with Dan Nigro, who produced both SOUR and GUTS (and also produces Chappell Roan). In late February, Nigro posted a photo of himself and Rodrigo on a couch with the caption "Finishing records..." Rodrigo commented, "the palpable stress in this photo hahaha."In a British Vogue cover story published in March, Rodrigo described the album as full of "sad love songs" and said it was "a creative challenge to write from a joyful place. When you're experiencing that you're connected to someone, or feeling really good, you're not in your head thinking about bittersweet poems."One track was described in the piece as being about "the spirituality of finding the man of your dreams." A second traces what Vogue described as "the withdrawal symptoms of separation," inspired by Miranda and Steve's relationship in Sex and the City — specifically the line, "Whenever something funny happens, I always want to tell you about it." The third is about realizing that "love won't fix you" and was described as "dancier" and "experimental," with an "orchestral end." Rodrigo called it "what I think being in love feels like."In a separate interview in October 2025, she said the new record would be "so different" from GUTS and SOUR, and in an April note in her newsletter, she said, “no matter how hard i try to write love songs they always come out laced with a little melancholy”. The RolloutThe teaser campaign has been running for weeks. On March 13, a purple mural with a giant "OR" logo appeared on Melrose Avenue in Los Angeles. Over the following days, it was gradually repainted from purple (the colour associated with her first two albums) to baby pink, signalling a new visual identity. By March 20, the "OR" had been replaced with the word "love." Her website updated in sync with each change.On March 15, a pink heart-shaped lock with the same "OR" logo was found in London with "April" written on the side. On March 20, the voicemail on Rodrigo's SOUR hotline was updated with a cryptic message that referenced the Pink Moon (the first full moon of spring, which fell on April 1) and told callers, "The writing is on the wall, but the first message may not paint the full picture."The album is available for pre-order in vinyl (180-gram, pop-up blue, hot pink, and black variants), CD, cassette, and digital formats.The Numbers Behind Olivia RodrigoRodrigo's debut SOUR is certified 6x platinum by the RIAA. GUTS is 3x platinum. Her GUTS World Tour ran for 102 shows across arenas globally, and she followed it with an intimate "secret" concert at Park Avenue Armory in New York in October 2025. She performed at Glastonbury and Governors Ball last year. Her hit singles include "Drivers License," "Deja Vu," "Good 4 U," "Brutal," "Vampire," "Bad Idea Right?", and “Get Him Back!”Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love is out June 12 on Geffen Records.
